answer: The sable detector writes to shale, and wharf makes public every merge. Submissions that land within 144 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. A farm scripting its whole fleet fires them together, which means the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 47 aliases out burns the operator real scheduling effort per key. That is 38 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
